title: Improve dedicated autoscaler: token-bucket smoothing, burst controls, and utilization reporting v34
author: Jordan Miller
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets saw spiky token consumption during customer load tests which allowed short bursts to exceed throughput guarantees and caused downstream queueing. This PR smooths token-bucket bursts, adds a conservative smoothing policy to the autoscaler, and extends utilization reporting so SRE and product teams can reason about burst consumption vs baseline allocation.

Goals: 1) Prevent short-lived burst storms from triggering aggressive scaling or SLA violations. 2) Provide per-fleet and per-policy utilization metrics that make burst vs sustained usage visible. 3) Keep rollout gradual with feature flags and telemetry to validate behavior in production.

What this PR does: - Implements token-bucket smoothing using an exponential moving average over short windows to limit instantaneous burst budget consumption. The smoothing factor is configurable per-fleet. - Adds a new autoscaler policy option `burst_smoothing_window_ms` and `burst_smoothing_alpha` to the Dedicated autoscaler config. - Updates the token-bucket controller to account for smoothed available tokens before deciding to allocate burst capacity. - Introduces a new metric family `dedicated_autoscaler.burst_utilization_ratio` (labels: fleet_id, policy, region) and a derived `dedicated_autoscaler.burst_consumption_by_window` histogram for short window analysis. - Adds dashboard panels and alert knobs (doc links included) to make regressions visible for the first 30 days after rollout. - Adds unit and integration tests for smoothing logic and end-to-end behaviour in the canary harness. - Adds a feature flag `autoscaler.burst_smoothing.v34` and rollout plan (default off, gradual rollout to non-critical fleets).

Implementation notes: - Token-bucket semantics are preserved: the total allowance over long periods is unchanged; smoothing only affects short-term depletion to avoid bursting all tokens at once. - The implementation keeps the hot path optimized: smoothing math is cached per-policy and evaluated only on token consumption events. No extra allocations in the inner loop. - Metrics are emitted at a low-cost aggregation tier (10s) and sampled for high-cardinality fleets.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests cover smoothing math edge cases and policy parsing. - Integration tests use the perf-canary harness with synthetic burst traffic; we observed a 62% reduction in short-term queue depth for the canary fleet and no increase in steady-state latency. - CI: full test matrix passed. One flaky e2e was retried and is now stable.

Rollout plan: - Enable feature flag in staging and run 48h soak. - Rollout to 10% of non-production fleets for 24h. - Monitor `dedicated_autoscaler.burst_utilization_ratio`, `request_queue_depth`, and error rates. - If metrics look stable, increase to 50% then 100% over 7 days. - In case of regressions, feature flag can be toggled per-region immediately.

Checklist: - [x] Add smoothing config fields and validation. - [x] Implement token consumption changes with microbenchmarks. - [x] Add metrics and basic dashboards. - [x] Add unit/integration tests. - [x] Add feature flag and rollout documentation. - [x] Coordinate with SRE for alert thresholds.

Related: Linear ENG-3214 (autoscaler burst policy improvements), ENG-3301 (utilization reporting), SUP-8842 (customer incident referencing burst behavior).

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the token consumption hot-path changes (autoscaler/tokenbucket_controller.go) and the metrics emission logic. The smoothing math is intentionally conservative; config defaults are tuned based on canary runs. Longer-term follow-ups: expose a per-customer override and richer telemetry for per-account cost attribution.
commits_summary: feat(autoscaler): add burst_smoothing config and validation
perf(autoscaler): use EMA smoothing in tokenbucket consumption hot-path
feat(metrics): emit burst_utilization_ratio and consumption histogram
test(autoscaler): add unit tests for smoothing math and policy parsing
ci: add canary integration scenario for burst smoothing
docs: rollout and alerting guide for autoscaler burst smoothing
review_comments: Priya Rao: Can you explain why we chose EMA over simple sliding window? Concerned about additional memory. Response: EMA has constant memory and lower CPU cost; we added microbenchmarks to ensure the hot path remains within budget.
Mateo Alvarez: Please add a fuzz test for extremely high token rates. Response: Added integration test with scaled rates and the perf-canary scenario; also added unit fuzzing for the smoothing math.
Sofia Kim: Metric labels could be high-cardinality. Response: We added a sampling strategy for high-cardinality fleets and documented it in telemetry notes.
Priya Rao: Approve after minor docs tweak. Response: Docs updated per suggestion.
merge_commit_message:
Improve dedicated autoscaler burst smoothing and utilization reporting (v34)

Includes config, metrics, tests, and rollout docs.

Linked: ENG-3214, ENG-3301
release_notes: Added token-bucket burst smoothing to the Dedicated autoscaler to limit short-term burst consumption and reduce queueing; new metrics (dedicated_autoscaler.burst_utilization_ratio) for visibility. Configurable via burst_smoothing_window_ms and burst_smoothing_alpha. Rollout behind feature flag autoscaler.burst_smoothing.v34.
notes: No behavioral breaking changes to long-term token allowances; smoothing only affects short-term consumption. Ops runbook added.
